note: Added by session 6a232e79-nfl1. These items are proposals and questions. Nothing here has been implemented. Each suggestion needs a human choice before any change is made to the data, the model or the live pages.

questions.question: Is there an official source for depth charts for all 32 clubs?
questions.known: nfl.com depth-chart URL for Washington returns 404 (re-checked 2026-11-12). The chiefs.com page is titled 'Unofficial Depth Chart'.
questions.unknown: Whether any club or league page publishes a labelled official depth chart for the other 29 clubs.
questions.discovery: Read each of the 32 club depth-chart pages; record the page title, the label, the 'as of' date, and the status code.
questions.blocks: Any league-wide 2nd, 3rd and 4th-string tracking (brief item: injuries and depth).

questions.question: When does the official injury page publish game statuses (Out, Doubtful, Questionable) relative to kickoff?
questions.known: On the Week 10 page, 6 of 279 rows carry a game status; the rest have practice status only. Official news (Darnold, ruled out) runs ahead of the page's game-status column.
questions.unknown: The publication schedule for game statuses in Week 10, and whether news and page agree at kickoff.
questions.discovery: Snapshot the page Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday morning; record each change with its time.
questions.blocks: Any availability feature that depends on the game designation.

questions.question: Why does the injury scrape change between refreshes (279 rows some runs, 295 others), and what stops a bad run being published?
questions.known: The injury scrape has been 279 of 279 on some refreshes (22:30Z; 22:40:41Z on 9040190) and 242 of 279 with 16 extra rows on others (22:36Z; 22:40:44Z on main 89ecd84). Live page re-read: 80 of 80 rows match the transcription.
questions.unknown: The parser change behind the 22:36Z result, and whether any change to the parser is still needed.
questions.discovery: Diff pipeline/scrape_injuries.py output across the three refreshes; re-run tools/verify_official_injuries.py on each.
questions.blocks: Trusting any single refresh without the per-refresh check.

questions.question: Is there a licensed source for closing or current betting lines that can be cited?
questions.known: No official nfl.com betting lines were found on the pages read. The repo's line data is a third-party mirror (F02).
questions.unknown: Whether a licensed or published feed exists, and under what terms it may be cited.
questions.discovery: Check the terms of each candidate feed; record whether lines are closing or current, and the timestamp.
questions.blocks: Every market-based value on the lines and strategy pages (left blank until resolved).

questions.question: How many tests make up the Benjamini-Hochberg family, and does the family include the 12 strategies only?
questions.known: The published q-values reproduce from the 12 published p-values (standard BH).
questions.unknown: Whether other rules were tested and not published (researcher degrees of freedom).
questions.discovery: Log every rule tested, including rejected ones, with a date. Publish the count next to the q-values.
questions.blocks: Any claim that a strategy beats chance after correction.

questions.question: Do own lines beat the market out of sample with a margin that is larger than the noise?
questions.known: 2026 test (136 games): model spread MAE 9.98 vs market 9.49; model weight negative (model output, unverified).
questions.unknown: Performance over a larger out-of-sample window with a pre-stated margin.
questions.discovery: Pre-register the margin and the window; add seasons only as they complete; report the interval of the difference.
questions.blocks: Any 'edge' or 'actionable' label on the lines page.

questions.question: Are the 12 strategies distinct bets?
questions.known: S04 and S06 share 207 games with correlation 1.0 (model output, unverified).
questions.unknown: Correlation on the full bet series, with zeros for games not bet.
questions.discovery: Build a bet matrix over all games and compute pairwise correlation on it.
questions.blocks: Gate G8 (diversification) and any portfolio claim.

questions.question: Which official source states the rules on who may be listed as injured, and on when a player is removed from the report (for example, injured reserve)?
questions.known: The official page lists current-week rows; news on the same page reports injured-reserve moves (e.g., Lamar Jackson IR, Malik Willis IR).
questions.unknown: The league's stated reporting rule for players placed on IR during the week.
questions.discovery: Read the official injury-report policy and the game-day report rules; record the section and date.
questions.blocks: Interpreting 'No Injuries Reported' for BAL and LAC.

suggestions.title: Add a per-refresh gate: fail the data build when the injury scrape differs from the official page by row count or any field.
suggestions.decision_impact: Stops a bad refresh being published, as happened at 22:36Z.

suggestions.title: Replace 'Starters flagged 103 — official game status' with two labelled numbers: official game designations (6) and practice-only starters (112).
suggestions.decision_impact: Stops an official-sounding label from covering a model assumption.

suggestions.title: Choose a depth-chart source for all 32 clubs: (a) scrape each club's depth-chart page and keep its label; (b) use a third-party weekly depth release as a cross-check only; (c) keep three clubs and say so.
suggestions.decision_impact: Decides whether 2nd, 3rd and 4th-string tracking is possible at all.
suggestions.recommended_path: Decide: (a) with a label check, then (b) as a cross-check

suggestions.title: Remove the 'actionable' label until the model beats the market out of sample by a pre-stated margin.
suggestions.decision_impact: Stops a negative validation result being shown as a signal.

suggestions.title: Merge duplicate strategies (S04 and S06) and compute diversification on the full bet series.
suggestions.decision_impact: Removes a false source of diversification.

suggestions.title: Require G5 (significance) for any status above FAIL, or rename WATCH.
suggestions.decision_impact: Stops WATCH implying significance when G5 fails.
suggestions.recommended_path: Decide between requiring G5 and renaming the status

suggestions.title: Choose one canonical site and archive the other generations under legacy/ with a notice (RV-17, RV-21).
suggestions.decision_impact: Removes conflicting pages; changes existing links.

suggestions.title: Add a news-to-status reconciliation: when official news reports an absence, flag the matching injury row until the page catches up.
suggestions.decision_impact: Closes the gap seen with Darnold (news ahead of the page).
